annotation.title_clean: Could the destruction of a beloved robot be considered a hate crime? An exploration of the legal and social significance of robot love
annotation.title_en: Could the destruction of a beloved robot be considered a hate crime? An exploration of the legal and social significance of robot love
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical-legal paper arguing that love for a social robot cannot ground legal protections or robot rights, since this would be unfair to the unloved. It argues the loss of a robot partner should be socially recognised as bereavement, and that destroying a beloved robot could be criminalised as a hate crime under certain conditions.
key_provisions_or_claims: Love for a robot cannot itself justify granting robot rights or special legal protection
Mamak's proposal to criminalise destruction of a robot partner is rejected as unfair to unloved entities
Loss of a robot partner should be socially validated as bereavement to avoid disenfranchised grief
Under certain conditions, destroying a beloved robot could be treated as a hate crime
